summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type 1 diabetes, depression, and a history of alcohol use, was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by nausea, vomiting, and missed insulin doses, compounded by alcohol consumption. She presented with severe hyperglycemia (glucose >1100), metabolic acidosis (pH 6.91), hyperkalemia (K+ 7.4), and hypotension requiring levophed. Treatment included IV fluids, insulin drip, sodium bicarbonate, and electrolyte management. Her condition stabilized over three days, with resolution of DKA and normalization of labs. She was transitioned back to subcutaneous insulin with an increased bedtime Lantus dose. The patient expressed motivation to address her alcohol use, and outpatient rehab was arranged. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for diabetes, mental health, and substance use care.
